scope: Standalone production dispatch-policy and descriptor block for the pending CSR/MRET integration. Tests supply rename/ROB acceptance and validated recovery synthetically. Not yet connected to the production issue backend, head controller, PRF reads or frontend. No complete CSR instruction path, formal acceptance or clock claim.
dispatch: valid_i is a lane-zero prefix. system_i classifies CSR/MRET after frontend-fault override; cfi0_i classifies the selected lane-zero CFI. Ordinary pairs pass through. Lane-zero CSR/MRET is admitted alone; lane-one CSR/MRET is deferred while lane zero proceeds. CFI lane zero cuts the tail. dispatch_valid_o is the offered backend prefix, not acceptance; all other resources must still reserve it atomically. Feed dispatch_solo_o into ROB allocation. Feed only queue_dispatch_o into IQ dispatch. Held ownership blocks all younger allocation, while previously admitted older IQ work may continue.
capture: On actual accepted lane-zero system allocation, save the full 13-bit ROB identity, original instruction/PC and renamed physical source tag. Lane-zero metadata inputs are ignored otherwise. The caller uses decode_single: register CSR reads its renamed rs1; immediate CSR, MRET and rs1=x0 use p0. A register CSR with rd=rs1 must retain its old source, not its new destination. Later RAT or offered-input changes cannot replace the captured source.
head: system_valid_o requires a held descriptor, live head, exact generation+slot identity and matching PC, with no reset/flush/drain/recovery. This qualifies later head-controller preparation and PRF read arbitration; it does not claim operand readiness. The controller must wait for the captured tag to be ready and use accepted-write bypass. The descriptor remains held through preparation, backpressure and an illegal completion.
release: Only actual legal serial retirement with matching full identity releases normally. No same-cycle descriptor refill or younger dispatch is allowed. Illegal completion does not release; accepted trap recovery must drive flush_i. Reset/full flush cancels ownership. CSR state itself is not part of this block.
recovery: recover_i denotes an already validated and accepted branch recovery; recover_slot_i is the branch slot and head_id_i supplies the pre-cycle head. Modulo-32 order kills only a younger descriptor, suppressing every new offer that cycle. Older/equal descriptors are retained. killed_o reports cancellation for the future head-controller connection. Full reset/flush dominates retirement. Slot-only recovery is valid only with upstream generation/live-branch validation. Recovery cannot coincide with accepted serial retirement.
drain: drained_i suppresses new transactions and requires no held descriptor. Coordinator must also check external IQ/producer/ROB/frontend holders; this block does not implement global identity drain.
